rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 - two-year field experiment (2005, 2006) in Bursa, Turkey with five drip irrigation treatments (T100-T0) measuring canopy temperature, soil water, ETc, yield and quality. Q2: Section 3.5 and Fig. 7, Table 3 - the authors fit a polynomial relationship between WUE and seasonal mean CWSI (R2 = 0.67, RMSE = 0.03) and state that the highest WUE is obtained at a CWSI value close to 0.6; Section 3.3 reports WUE was highest in T25 in both years. Q4: Sections 2, 3.1, 3.3 - ETc measured by soil water balance with neutron probe; WUE computed as seed yield/ETc; Fig. 1 and Fig. 4 show the yield-ETc and WUE-ETc relations, i.e. the components through which deficit scheduling raises WUE (ETc falls more than yield). Q8: Sections 3.3, 3.5 and 4 - authors caveat that the high-WUE strategy (T25, CWSI ~0.6) causes about 27.5% yield decrease and that economic aspects must be considered; thresholds are stated to hold only under the conditions of this study and with drip irrigation; Section 3.4 notes the observed VPD range (1-4 kPa) was narrower than recommended for baseline definition, and some CWSI values fell outside 0-1.
rows.notes: The technology label is 'app_scheduling', but the study uses a hand-held infrared thermometer to compute the empirical CWSI (Idso method) for scheduling; no app or automated system is involved. Since the passage itself describes exactly the study's own WUE-CWSI result, Q2 is rated yes, but the review's framing of this as an app-based technology goes beyond the study. Q3: WUE and CWSI each derived by a single method (soil water balance plus harvest; IRT) - no independent triangulation. Q5/Q6: single site, single crop (one cultivar), plot scale only. Q7: the statement that the strategy could be preferred under water scarcity or high water cost is an adoption context, not a stated requirement for the effect. Q9: only R2 and RMSE for the regression; no SD, CI or range for WUE values, no LSD for WUE.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a two-year, single-site field experiment on drip-irrigated soybean using the empirical CWSI for scheduling; its WUE-CWSI polynomial (max WUE at CWSI ~0.6) is reported directly in Section 3.5 / Fig. 7.
